content: The solubility of ledipasvir decreases as gastric pH increases. Consequently, medications that raise gastric pH are expected to reduce ledipasvir levels. Proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) at doses equivalent to omeprazole 20 mg or less can be administered with ledipasvir/sofosbuvir under fasting conditions, but close monitoring is recommended. Dexlansoprazole can increase the levels or effects of lemborexant by altering its metabolism through the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. If co-administered with weak CYP3A4 inhibitors, a lower nightly dose of lemborexant is recommended. Refer to the drug monograph for specific dosage adjustments. Lenacapavir, a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor, may increase the levels or effects of CYP3A4 substrates initiated within nine months after the last subcutaneous dose of lenacapavir, potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions. Lenacapavir also increases dexlansoprazole levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Dexlansoprazole decreases the levels or effects of levoketoconazole by increasing gastric pH, which applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Conversely, levoketoconazole may increase dexlansoprazole levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. These interactions are considered minor, with unclear clinical significance. Dexlansoprazole reduces the levels of levothyroxine, liothyronine, and liotrix by increasing gastric pH, which applies only to their oral forms. Conflicting evidence exists regarding the clinical significance of these interactions. Dexlansoprazole may alter the pharmacokinetics of amphetamine and dextroamphetamine by reducing gastric acidity, which decreases the time to maximum concentration (Tmax) without affecting the area under the curve (AUC). Monitor patients for changes in clinical effects and adjust therapy as needed. Dexlansoprazole increases the levels of lonafarnib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with weak CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce lonafarnib to its starting dose. Avoid co-administration with sensitive CYP3A substrates. Dexlansoprazole decreases the levels or effects of nilotinib, pazopanib, and pexidartinib by increasing gastric pH. These interactions apply only to oral forms and are significant due to the pH-dependent solubility of these drugs. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. Dexlansoprazole increases the levels of tacrolimus by competing for CYP2C19 metabolism, particularly in intermediate or poor metabolizers. Monitor tacrolimus blood concentrations closely. Dexlansoprazole may increase the risk of toxicity with methotrexate by reducing renal clearance, especially at higher methotrexate doses. Monitor closely for signs of toxicity. Dexlansoprazole decreases the levels of mycophenolate by increasing gastric pH, which applies to the oral form of mycophenolate mofetil but not the enteric-coated mycophenolate sodium formulation. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear. Dexlansoprazole is contraindicated with nelfinavir due to reduced nelfinavir absorption and conversion to its active metabolite, potentially leading to virologic failure and resistance. Dexlansoprazole decreases the levels of neratinib and sotorasib by increasing gastric pH. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. If unavoidable, adjust the timing of administration to minimize interaction. Dexlansoprazole increases the levels of midazolam (intranasal) by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially prolonging sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. Dexlansoprazole decreases the levels of thyroid desiccated by increasing gastric pH. Conflicting evidence exists regarding the clinical significance of this interaction. Dexlansoprazole increases the levels of tinidazole and triclabenazole by affecting CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 metabolism, respectively. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. Dexlansoprazole increases the levels of voriconazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Dexlansoprazole may cause serious side effects, including kidney problems (acute interstitial nephritis), antibiotic-associated diarrhea (Clostridioides difficile infection), severe skin reactions (Stevens-Johnson Syndrome or Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis), and Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms (DRESS). It may also worsen lupus, cause vitamin B12 deficiency, hypomagnesemia, and increase the risk of bone loss and fractures. Patients should be advised to report any concerning symptoms to their healthcare provider immediately. Dexlansoprazole is metabolized primarily by CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 enzymes. The drug is extensively metabolized in the liver, with excretion occurring via feces and urine. Dexlansoprazole is used to treat conditions such as gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and erosive esophagitis by reducing stomach acid production. It is available in delayed-release oral capsules (30 mg and 60 mg) and should be stored at room temperature. Common side effects include diarrhea, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, gas, and headache. Serious side effects should be reported to a healthcare provider.
